messages:
arjun: heads-up — after the kernel-selector change rolled yesterday we're seeing a non‑monotonic latency profile on llama-3-13b. p50 stable, p95 spiking ~40% on chat workloads.

maria: can you paste numbers? which selector commit? :eyes:

arjun: p50 ~120ms, p95 was ~360ms before deploy, now ~510ms. selector commit b3f9ea — it prefers `fused_attention_v2` for heads=32/hidden=4096 combos.

liam: interesting. any memcopy or KV-cache thrash in the trace? my gut says kernel mismatch causing extra copies on the slow path.

arjun: trace snippet:
```
[2026-03-15 09:12:03] alloc_kv_cache  -> 12.4ms
[2026-03-15 09:12:03] kernel(fused_attention_v2) -> 18.1ms
[2026-03-15 09:12:03] fallback(kernel=matmul_ep) -> 42.7ms
```
we're seeing occasional fallbacks to matmul_ep for some batch shapes.

maria: hmm — do the requests have mixed sequence lengths? selector might pick fused attention when avg_seq<512 but some requests are long and trigger fallback.

arjun: yes, chat template uses dynamic system+messages, tail tokens vary. Batching heuristics currently bucket by avg_seq. Maybe that causes mismatches inside a batch.

jess: quick idea — add an upper bound check in the selector: if max_seq > threshold force kernel that handles long sequences without fallback. Also verify rope_theta scaling assumptions since some kernels expect normalized RoPE.

liam: +1. Also we should check RMSNorm vs fused-RMSNorm+SiLU path. When hidden size is 4096 and head_dim 128 we enabled fused SiLU kernels; those have a slightly different memory layout and can force extra transpose.

arjun: verified: enabling `fused_rms_silu=true` in runtime toggles a different compute path and coincides with the spikes. When I pinned `fused_rms_silu=false` locally p95 drops to 380ms (still higher than baseline but much better).

maria: so two levers: kernel selection logic and fused RMSNorm. Which one is cheaper to change short term? runtime flag flip vs selector rollback?

jess: flip flag for canary hosts first. We can also add a quick selector patch: check per-request max_seq and head_dim compatibility before committing to fused_attention_v2. Patch should be safe and quick.

liam: let's capture a microbenchmark across shapes. Can someone run the new benchmark harness with these matrix sizes: hidden=4096, heads=32, seq=[64,128,512,1024], batch=[1,4,8]. Use `perf/bench_selector.sh --model llama-3-13b --kernels all` and upload traces.

arjun: running now on dc-gpu-23. attaching partial results:
```
shape h4096 heads32 seq64 b4  -> fused_attention_v2 (fast) p95 115ms
shape h4096 heads32 seq512 b4 -> fused_attention_v2 (fallback) p95 420ms
shape h4096 heads32 seq1024 b1 -> matmul_ep (direct) p95 380ms
```
so fused path falls back when seq512 present in batch.

maria: that confirms batching heuristic is the culprit. For chat we shouldn't mix <128 and >512 in same batch. Adjust heuristics to bucket by max_seq rather than avg_seq for kernels sensitive to seq.

jess: agree. Proposed rollout plan:
- canary flip fused_rms_silu=false on 10% of hosts
- patch selector to use max_seq threshold and prefer conservative kernel when mixed
- add instrumentation: `selector_reason` tag to traces so we know why kernel chosen

liam: add a metric for # of fallbacks and avg fallback penalty (time delta between chosen kernel and fallback). We'll alert if fallback count rises >5%.

arjun: one more note re: RoPE: some of the new attention kernels assume rope_theta=10000 normalization but our model manifests rope_theta=8192 in metadata. That mismatch can cause kernel to fallback to the 'generic' attention that does re-scaling and is slower.

maria: oh yikes. how did rope_theta drift? was it from the model conversion script?

arjun: likely — conversion tool defaults changed last month. I'll add a validation check at model-load time to warn if runtime kernel expects a different rope_theta. Quick fix is to expose `model_meta.rope_theta` to the selector and include it in kernel capability checks.

jess: perfect. Also let's add a short note to docs: "kernel compatibility matrix: required head_dim, rope_theta, fused_rms flag" so solutions engineers know why some kernels are chosen.

liam: action items assigned:
- arjun: patch model-load rope_theta validation + run full perf harness (ETA EOD)
- maria: update selector heuristic to use max_seq for kernel-sensitive kernels (ETA tomorrow am)
- jess: canary fused_rms_silu=false rollout + add selector_reason tag (ETA today)
- infra-bot: create dashboard with fallback_count, fallback_penalty_ms, top-fallback-kernel

infra-bot: created ticket INF-4921, dashboard: https://grafana.internal/r/INF-4921

arjun: thanks — I'll post updated bench results once full run finishes. If anything else pops up ping @maria @liam.

maria: thanks all :thumbsup:

liam: thanks — and good catch on rope_theta drift, that was subtle.
